title: Eight assertions for a finite biproduct with one prime annihilator
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring, k a field, X a scheme, and f:X→Spec k. Let r be prime, I a finite set, and G_a a family of constructible Λ-module sheaves on X_et, each killed by r (r times its identity morphism is zero). Let H be another such module sheaf with an isomorphism H ≅ ⨁_a G_a. Then the eight conditional predicates [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] satisfy Assertions Λ f H if and only if Assertions Λ f (G_a) for every a. The predicates are used as formally defined, without a curve or algebraic closedness hypothesis. The common-prime hypothesis concerns [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]; constructibility is [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. The empty family is allowed.

source.place: Theorem 03SC, proof, fourth paragraph; Lemma 0A5C. Primary text checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SC and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A5C.

proof.text: Install the component constructibility instances. Use Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf.biproduct and Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf.of_iso to prove H constructible. By biproduct.hom_ext', each injection composed with r times the identity is (r times the identity of its component) composed with that injection, hence zero. Cancel e.hom to transport the resulting annihilation to H.

Apply the three componentwise equivalences to C1,C2,C5,C7,C8; C3; and C4,C6. Unpack Assertions with assertions_iff. In each direction, use the corresponding implications of the three equivalences, distribute the finite conjunction over the universal quantifier, and repack all eight fields with assertions_iff.

theorem assertions_iff_of_prime_biproduct_iso (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ]
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (r : ℕ) [Fact r.Prime] {ι : Type} [Finite ι]
    (G : ι → Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (hGc : ∀ a, Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf (G a)) (hGr : ∀ a, r • 𝟙 (G a) = 0)
    {H : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)} (e : H ≅ ⨁ G) :
    Assertions Λ f H ↔ ∀ a, Assertions Λ f (G a)
